question: The function \(f(x)\) satisfies \(f(2+x)=f(2-x)\) for all real numbers \(x.\) If the equation \(f(x)=0\) has exactly four distinct real roots, then the sum of these roots is
solution:
The identity compares inputs equally far from \(2\), suggesting that roots occur at reflected positions. If \(r\) is a root, substitute \(x=r-2\) into the identity to get
\[
f(r)=f(4-r)=0.
\]
Thus \(4-r\) is also a root.

Write all four distinct roots in increasing order as \(r_1<r_2<r_3<r_4\). Their four reflected values are distinct roots too, so they form the same complete list in reverse order. Consequently
\[
4-r_1=r_4,
\qquad
4-r_2=r_3.
\]
Each resulting pair sums to \(4\). Hence the sum of all four roots is
\[
(r_1+r_4)+(r_2+r_3)=4+4=\boxed{8},
\]
choice E.
